newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan continued its upward trend on Friday to close at 8.2945 against the U.S. dollar, from Thursday's 8.2960, due to some active buying late in the trading session, traders said.

The yuan opened higher at 8.2948 and fell quickly to its intra-day low of 8.2960. The currency then rose slightly to move around 8.2952 for the rest of the session, reaching an intra-day high of 8.2910.
Trading was active, with most business done at the 8.2952 level, traders said.
Dealers said buying tested resistance at 8.2950, as it did on Thursday, and successfully closed above that level this time.
Although the market expected the central bank to cap the currency's rise at about 8.2950, there was no sign of intervention, a dealer said.
"The yuan was pushed higher by good bids during the final fifteen minutes of trading," he added.
But a second dealer said the market was unsure about whether the currency could keep its head above 8.2950 on Monday.
He said the yuan could continue its slow move upwards if the central bank does not intervene.
Dealers expected the yuan to struggle around 8.2950 early next week.
The yuan bounced down to close at 6.9600 from 6.9401 against 100 Japanese yen. It closed up at 1.0714 from 1.0720 against the Hong Kong dollar.
